subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee credential isolation for arbitrary agent-executed tools in core, and if so, which execution boundary is authoritative enough that the model and ordinary tool results never receive raw values?
rationale: Current main deliberately documents SecretRefs as storage and egress hardening rather than process isolation. Choosing a stronger guarantee changes the trust model, execution architecture, plugin contract, and compatibility surface, so automation cannot safely select it.

options.title: Core broker boundary
options.body: Add a generic core dispatch-time credential broker with exact-value redaction and plugin-backed providers while keeping agent-visible command arguments and environments secret-free.

options.title: Isolation-only contract
options.body: Keep SecretRefs as the supported core mechanism and formally require OS/container isolation or external proxies for credentials used by arbitrary commands.

options.title: Plugin-first experiment
options.body: Standardize only the minimum SDK seam required for external credential-vault plugins, then reconsider a core guarantee after production proof.

recommendation.title: Core broker boundary
recommendation.body: Add a generic core dispatch-time credential broker with exact-value redaction and plugin-backed providers while keeping agent-visible command arguments and environments secret-free.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent implementation history across SecretRef runtime, gateway resolution, audit, migration, tests, and documentation.
